extracted.intended_audience: public relations students and practitioners (PR writers, media-relations professionals, communications officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Format- and ethics-focused rules for drafting press releases and closely related PR documents (media advisories, fact sheets, backgrounders) that maximize media pickup and reduce legal/risk exposure. Covers classical newsroom expectations and emerging-media distribution formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: News release vs. media advisory distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: A news release announces news (a happening, a finding, an action), whereas a media advisory invites attendance (a press conference, an event).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mix the two in one document — combining an announcement and an invitation confuses editors and reduces pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact sheet vs. backgrounder
rubrics_metrics.description: A fact sheet is bulleted, telegraphic, and scannable; a backgrounder is narrative and provides context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement the release with the appropriate companion document (use a fact sheet for quick facts and a backgrounder for deeper context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted-pyramid lead discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead (first sentence/paragraph) must answer the W's (who, what, when, where, why); subsequent paragraphs add detail in descending importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow strict lead discipline so journalists can quickly identify the news and trim from the bottom if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct quotes must be attributed to named, titled individuals (e.g., 'Lead author Dr. Y, Professor of Z at University W'), not generic labels like 'a spokesperson' or 'an executive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position titles for journalists' benefit; avoid anonymous or fabricated quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-interest tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases distributed nationally should include local-interest variants for community papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create localized angles or datelines so regional outlets can see relevance to their audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date and time stamping
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases must prominently display the date of issue and any embargo time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make embargo instructions clear and visible to avoid confusion and premature publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo/video inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Visuals (photos, video) are treated as baseline requirements, not optional extras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always supply suitable high-quality visual assets to increase pickup and story friendliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of release identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the type of release (announcement, response, feature, hometown, financial, crisis, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the format conventions for each type — structure, tone, and required content differ by release type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth in publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements presented as fact must be verifiable; opinions should be confined to quoted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure factual claims can be substantiated to preserve credibility and avoid misleading journalists/audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of deceptive practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use fake quotes, astroturfing, or conceal sponsorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparent authorship and sourcing; deceptive tactics risk reputational and legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Named individuals quoted in a release must have given express consent; special protections apply to minors and patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and document consent for quotes and personal information; redact or avoid sensitive personal data when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamation risk audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases that name or discuss third parties should be screened for libel risk, particularly when competitors are mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a basic legal risk review before distribution to avoid defamatory statements and potential litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted text from published sources, photographs, and graphics must be properly licensed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure usage rights or permissions for third-party content and credit sources appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow applicable disclosure rules (SEC, FTC, FDA, and similar regulators) when releases touch regulated matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify regulator-driven disclosure requirements early and include required statements or filings to remain compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-platform format
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare release versions for multiple platforms: blog, website, email, social (Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Facebook), photo (Instagram), and video (YouTube/TikTok).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor format, length, and assets to each channel rather than simply copying the same document across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hashtag coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide suggested hashtags and synchronize the release with the issuer's social media plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include coordinated campaign tags to increase discoverability and alignment across social posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed-friendly content
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply tweets, videos, and quotes as embeddable content blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for digital publishers to embed multimedia and quoted excerpts by providing ready-to-use embed code or links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-first formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Release pages must render correctly on phone screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize headings, paragraph length, visuals, and file sizes for mobile consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search-engine signaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines should signal the news in a search-friendly way, placing key terms in the first ~60 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write concise, descriptive headlines that surface relevant keywords early for SEO and social previews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wiki-citation consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If a release may seed Wikipedia entries, supply citation-friendly facts and verifiable secondary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide RFC-style, neutral factual statements and links to independent sources to facilitate encyclopedic use without promotional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness as format + risk reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: A pickup-worthy modern release satisfies newsroom intake expectations and emerging-media format needs while minimizing legal and ethical risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine classical release conventions (inverted pyramid, clear attribution, appropriate companion docs) with multi-platform, embed-friendly, mobile-first formatting and perform ethics/legal checks — outlets deprioritize releases that pose legal or reputational risks.
